chapters.title: The Book Read in Babylon
chapters.html:
Baruch 1

1These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,

2in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire.

3Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book,

4in the hearing of the nobles and the king's sons, in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, all who lived in Babylon by the river Sud.

5They wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord,

6and they collected money, as much as each could give,

7and sent it to Jerusalem, to Jehoiakim the priest, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, and to the priests and to all the people who were found with him in Jerusalem.

8This was when he received the vessels of the house of the Lord that had been carried away from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah, on the tenth day of Sivan: the silver vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made

9after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away from Jerusalem Jeconiah and the princes, the prisoners, the nobles and the people of the land, and brought him to Babylon.

10They said: "We are sending you money. With the money buy burnt offerings and sin offerings and incense, and prepare a grain offering, and offer them on the altar of the Lord our God;

11and pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and for the life of Belshazzar his son, that their days on earth may be like the days of heaven.

12The Lord will give us strength and light to our eyes, and we will live under the shadow of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and under the shadow of Belshazzar his son, and serve them many days and find favor in their sight.

13Pray for us also to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and to this day the anger of the Lord and His wrath have not turned away from us.

14You shall read this book that we are sending you, to make confession in the house of the Lord on the day of the feast and on the days of the appointed seasons.

The Confession

15You shall say: To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as at this day: to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,

16to our kings and our princes, to our priests and our prophets, and to our fathers,

17because we have sinned before the Lord

18and disobeyed Him, and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the commandments of the Lord that He set before us.

19From the day the Lord brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt until this day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and we have been quick to stop listening to His voice.

20So the calamities and the curse have clung to us, which the Lord declared through Moses His servant on the day He brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day.

21We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God in all the words of the prophets whom He sent to us,

22but each of us went after the thoughts of his own evil heart, to serve other gods and to do what is evil in the sight of the Lord our God."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah… in Babylon, in the fifth year" — Jeremiah's scribe, Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah (Jeremiah 32:12), here in Babylon with the exiles. The book survives in Greek. It dates itself to the fifth year, without saying of what, and names the day but not the month.

  • vv8–9 "the silver vessels that Zedekiah… had made" — in Jeremiah the false prophets promised that the vessels of the LORD's house will now shortly be brought back from Babylon (Jeremiah 27:16). Here vessels do go back: silver ones that Zedekiah had made.

  • vv11–12 "pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar… we will live under the shadow of Nebuchadnezzar" — Jeremiah's letter told the exiles to pray to the LORD on its behalf (Jeremiah 29:7). Under the shadow was what Jerusalem said of its own king, Under his shadow we shall live among the nations (Lamentations 4:20); now the shadow is Babylon's.

  • vv15–22 "To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as at this day" — the confession runs from here to 3:8, and much of it follows Daniel's prayer in the same words (Daniel 9:7–19). It confesses for every rank in turn, our kings and our princes, our priests and our prophets, and our fathers.

  • v20 "the calamities and the curse… which the Lord declared through Moses… a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day" — the curses of the law (Deuteronomy 28), and Jeremiah's own words, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day (Jeremiah 11:5).

chapters.title: To Us Shame of Face
chapters.html:
Baruch 2

1So the Lord has carried out the word that He spoke against us, and against our judges who judged Israel, against our kings and our princes, and against the men of Israel and Judah.

2Under the whole heaven nothing has been done like what He has done in Jerusalem, in keeping with what is written in the law of Moses,

3that we should eat, one the flesh of his son and another the flesh of his daughter.

4He has made them subject to all the kingdoms around us, a reproach and a desolation among all the peoples around, where the Lord has scattered them.

5They were put beneath and not above, because we sinned against the Lord our God by not listening to His voice.

6To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us and our fathers shame of face, as at this day.

7All these calamities that the Lord pronounced against us have come upon us.

8Yet we have not entreated the favor of the Lord by turning, each of us, from the thoughts of his evil heart.

9So the Lord has kept watch over the calamities, and the Lord has brought them upon us; for the Lord is righteous in all His works that He has commanded us.

10We have not listened to His voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord that He set before us.

11And now, Lord God of Israel, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders, with great power and an uplifted arm, and made Yourself a name, as at this day:

12we have sinned, we have been ungodly, we have done wrong, Lord our God, against all Your ordinances.

13Let Your anger turn away from us, for we are left few among the nations where You have scattered us.

14Hear, Lord, our prayer and our plea; deliver us for Your own sake, and grant us favor in the sight of those who have carried us into exile,

15so that all the earth may know that You are the Lord our God, for Your name is called over Israel and over his descendants.

16Lord, look down from Your holy house and consider us; incline Your ear, Lord, and hear.

17Open Your eyes, Lord, and see: it is not the dead in Hades, whose breath has been taken from their bodies, who will give glory and justice to the Lord;

18but the soul that grieves greatly, that walks bent over and feeble, the eyes that fail, and the soul that hungers, will give You glory and righteousness, Lord.

19For it is not because of any righteous deeds of our fathers and our kings that we lay our plea for mercy before You, Lord our God.

20For You have sent Your anger and Your wrath upon us, as You spoke through Your servants the prophets, saying:

21"This is what the Lord says: Bend your shoulders and serve the king of Babylon, and you will remain in the land that I gave to your fathers.

22But if you will not listen to the voice of the Lord and serve the king of Babylon,

23I will make to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the whole land will become a desolation without inhabitant."

24But we did not listen to Your voice, to serve the king of Babylon; and You carried out Your words, which You spoke through Your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be brought out of their place.

25They lie exposed to the heat by day and to the frost by night. They died in great misery, by famine, by sword and by pestilence.

26The house that is called by Your name You have made what it is today, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

27Yet You have dealt with us, Lord our God, in all Your kindness and in all Your great compassion,

28as You spoke through Your servant Moses on the day You commanded him to write Your law before the sons of Israel, saying:

29"If you will not listen to My voice, this great swarming multitude will surely be turned into a small number among the nations where I will scatter them.

30For I knew that they would not listen to Me, for they are a stiff-necked people. But in the land of their exile they will take it to heart,

31and they will know that I am the Lord their God. I will give them a heart and ears that hear,

32and they will praise Me in the land of their exile and remember My name;

33they will turn from their stiff neck and from their wicked deeds, for they will remember the way of their fathers, who sinned before the Lord.

34I will bring them back to the land that I swore to their fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, and they will rule over it; I will multiply them, and they will not be diminished.

35I will make an everlasting covenant with them, to be their God, and they will be My people; and I will never again remove My people Israel from the land that I have given them."

Notes

  • vv2–3 "nothing has been done like what He has done in Jerusalem… that we should eat, one the flesh of his son" — the curse written in the law, You will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters (Deuteronomy 28:53), which Lamentations saw fulfilled (Lamentations 4:10).

  • v5 "They were put beneath and not above" — the blessing of the law turned around: you will be only on top and not underneath, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 28:13).

  • v9 "the Lord has kept watch over the calamities" — the word of Jeremiah's almond branch, I am watching over My word to do it (Jeremiah 1:12), and of its last use, I will watch over them for harm and not for good (44:27).

  • v13 "we are left few among the nations" — the law's word, you will be left few in number among the nations (Deuteronomy 4:27).

  • vv17–18 "it is not the dead in Hades… but the soul that grieves… will give You glory" — The dead do not praise Yah (Psalm 115:17), and Sheol does not thank You (Isaiah 38:18). Hades is the Greek for Sheol. The prayer argues that the living, broken as they are, can still give God praise.

  • vv21–23 "Bend your shoulders and serve the king of Babylon… the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride" — Jeremiah's counsel, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him (Jeremiah 27:12), and his sentence, I will silence… the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride (7:34).

  • vv24–25 "the bones of our kings… exposed to the heat by day and to the frost by night… by pestilence" — Jeremiah 8:1, they will bring out of their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, and his word on Jehoiakim's body, thrown out to the heat by day and to the frost by night (36:30). Apostolē, "sending," stands for "pestilence" in the Greek Jeremiah too (Greek 39:36, Hebrew 32:36), in the same three: sword, famine and pestilence.

  • vv29–31 "a small number among the nations… in the land of their exile they will take it to heart… I will give them a heart and ears that hear" — the law's own promise after the curse: you take them to heart among all the nations (Deuteronomy 30:1), undoing the LORD has not given you a heart to know… or ears to hear (29:4).

  • v35 "an everlasting covenant… to be their God, and they will be My people" — Jeremiah's new covenant, I will be their God, and they will be My people (Jeremiah 31:33), and an everlasting covenant (32:40).

chapters.title: Where Is Wisdom?
chapters.html:
Baruch 3

1Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a soul in anguish and a weary spirit cries out to You.

2Hear, Lord, and have mercy, for we have sinned before You.

3For You are enthroned forever, and we are perishing forever.

4Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear now the prayer of the dead of Israel, the sons of those who sinned before You, who did not listen to Your voice, the voice of their God, so that calamities have clung to us.

5Do not remember the iniquities of our fathers, but remember Your hand and Your name at this time.

6For You are the Lord our God, and we will praise You, Lord.

7For this is why You have put the fear of You in our hearts: so that we would call on Your name. We will praise You in our exile, for we have put away from our hearts all the iniquity of our fathers who sinned before You.

8We are here today in our exile, where You have scattered us, to be a reproach and a curse and a penalty, for all the iniquities of our fathers, who turned away from the Lord our God.

Wisdom

9Hear, Israel, the commandments of life;
give ear to learn understanding!

10Why is it, Israel,
why is it that you are in the land of your enemies,
that you have grown old in a foreign land,
that you are defiled with the dead,

11that you are counted with those in Hades?

12You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom.

13If you had walked in the way of God,
you would be living in peace forever.

14Learn where there is understanding,
where there is strength, where there is insight,
so that you may also know where there is length of days and life,
where there is light for the eyes, and peace.

15Who has found her place?
Who has entered her storehouses?

16Where are the rulers of the nations,
and those who lorded it over the beasts on the earth,

17who made sport with the birds of the air,
who hoarded silver and gold,
in which people trust,
and whose getting had no end?

18For those who worked in silver and were anxious over it,
whose works are past finding out —

19they have vanished and gone down to Hades,
and others have risen up in their place.

20Younger men have seen the light
and lived on the earth,
but they have not known the way to knowledge,

21nor understood her paths,
nor laid hold of her;
their sons have strayed far from her way.

22She has not been heard of in Canaan,
nor seen in Teman;

23the sons of Hagar, who seek understanding on the earth,
the merchants of Merran and of Teman,
the storytellers and the seekers of understanding,
have not known the way of wisdom,
nor remembered her paths.

24O Israel, how great is the house of God,
how vast the place of His possession!

25It is great and has no end;
it is high and immeasurable.

26The giants were born there, famous from the beginning,
great in stature, skilled in war.

27God did not choose them,
nor give them the way to knowledge;

28they perished because they had no understanding;
they perished through their folly.

29Who has gone up into heaven and taken her,
and brought her down from the clouds?

30Who has gone over the sea and found her,
and will buy her for choice gold?

31No one knows the way to her,
or thinks about her path.

32But He who knows all things knows her;
He found her by His understanding.
He who prepared the earth for all time
filled it with four-footed creatures;

33He sends out the light, and it goes;
He called it, and it obeyed Him with trembling;

34the stars shone in their watches and were glad;

35He called them, and they said, "Here we are!"
They shone with gladness for Him who made them.

36This is our God;
no other can be compared to Him.

37He found out the whole way to knowledge
and gave it to Jacob His servant,
and to Israel, whom He loved.

38Afterward she appeared on earth
and lived among people.

Notes

  • vv3–4, 10–11 "we are perishing forever… the prayer of the dead of Israel… counted with those in Hades" — You are enthroned forever is the last prayer of Lamentations, You, LORD, are enthroned forever (Lamentations 5:19). The exiles call themselves the dead, and the poem that follows says the same: in a foreign land they are defiled with the dead and counted with those in Hades. Those who pray here are the living who, as 2:17–18 said, can still give God glory.

  • v9 "Hear, Israel, the commandments of life" — the confession ends, and a poem on wisdom begins (3:9–4:4), opening with the words of the law, Hear, Israel (Deuteronomy 6:4), and its choice, I have set before you today life and good (30:15).

  • v12 "You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom" — Jeremiah's charge, they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters (Jeremiah 2:13), with wisdom in place of the living waters.

  • vv15, 29–31 "Who has found her place?… Who has gone up into heaven and taken her… Who has gone over the sea and found her?" — Job's question, where is the place of understanding? (Job 28:12), and the law's word about the commandment, Who will go up for us to the heavens… Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea (Deuteronomy 30:12–13). The law said the commandment was near; Baruch says wisdom was out of reach until God gave it.

  • vv22–23 "nor seen in Teman… the merchants of Merran and of Teman" — Teman's wisdom was proverbial: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? (Jeremiah 49:7). The sons of Hagar are the peoples of Ishmael; Merran is otherwise unknown.

  • vv26–28 "The giants were born there, famous from the beginning" — the giants of the flood story, which the Greek of Genesis 6:4 calls the giants and the famous men, for the Hebrew Nephilim and the men of the name. Strength without wisdom perished.

  • vv33–35 "He called them, and they said, 'Here we are!'" — the stars answer as the lightnings in God's question to Job, Can you send out lightnings, so that they go and say to you, "Here we are"? (Job 38:35), and as in Isaiah, calling them all by name (Isaiah 40:26).

  • v36 "This is our God; no other can be compared to Him" — Isaiah's question, To whom then will you liken God? (Isaiah 40:18), answered.

  • v38 "Afterward she appeared on earth and lived among people" — the Greek verbs have no stated subject. Read with the poem, the subject is wisdom, who is the book of the commandments of God in the next verse (4:1); read with vv32–37, it is God, who found out the whole way to knowledge, and the verse says that God Himself appeared on earth and lived among people.

chapters.title: Take Courage, My People
chapters.html:
Baruch 4

1She is the book of the commandments of God,
the law that endures forever.
All who hold fast to her will live,
but those who forsake her will die.

2Turn, Jacob, and take hold of her;
walk toward her radiance, in the presence of her light.

3Do not give your glory to another,
or what is good for you to a foreign nation.

4Happy are we, Israel,
for what pleases God is made known to us.

Take Courage

5Take courage, my people,
you who keep alive the name of Israel!

6You were sold to the nations,
but not for destruction;
because you angered God,
you were handed over to your enemies.

7For you provoked Him who made you
by sacrificing to demons and not to God.

8You forgot the everlasting God, who brought you up,
and you grieved Jerusalem, who reared you.

9For she saw the anger that came upon you from God, and she said:
"Listen, you neighbors of Zion;
God has brought great mourning upon me.

10For I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters,
which the Everlasting brought upon them.

11With joy I nurtured them,
but with weeping and mourning I sent them away.

12Let no one rejoice over me,
a widow, forsaken by many;
I have been left desolate because of the sins of my children,
because they turned away from the law of God,

13and did not know His ordinances,
nor walk in the ways of God's commandments,
nor tread the paths of discipline in His righteousness.

14Let the neighbors of Zion come;
remember the captivity of my sons and daughters,
which the Everlasting brought upon them.

15For He brought against them a nation from far away,
a shameless nation of a strange language,
who had no respect for the old
and no pity for the child.

16They led away the widow's beloved sons
and left her alone, bereft of her daughters.

17But I — how can I help you?

18For He who brought these calamities upon you
will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.

19Go, my children, go;
for I have been left desolate.

20I have taken off the robe of peace
and put on the sackcloth of my supplication;
I will cry to the Everlasting all my days.

21Take courage, my children; cry to God,
and He will deliver you from tyranny, from the hand of your enemies.

22For I have put my hope in the Everlasting for your salvation,
and joy has come to me from the Holy One,
because of the mercy that will soon come to you
from your everlasting Savior.

23For I sent you out with mourning and weeping,
but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever.

24For as the neighbors of Zion have now seen your captivity,
so they will soon see your salvation from your God,
which will come to you with great glory
and with the splendor of the Everlasting.

25My children, bear patiently the anger that has come upon you from God.
Your enemy has pursued you,
but you will soon see his destruction
and will set your foot on their necks.

26My tender ones have traveled rough roads;
they were carried off like a flock seized by enemies.

27Take courage, my children, and cry to God,
for He who brought this upon you will remember you.

28For as your mind was set on going astray from God,
turn now and seek Him with ten times the zeal.

29For He who brought these calamities upon you
will bring you everlasting joy with your salvation."

Take Courage, Jerusalem

30Take courage, Jerusalem,
for He who named you will comfort you.

31Wretched are those who mistreated you
and rejoiced at your fall;

32wretched are the cities that your children served as slaves;
wretched is she who received your sons.

33For just as she rejoiced at your fall
and was glad at your ruin,
so she will grieve at her own desolation.

34I will take away her joy in her crowds,
and her boasting will be turned to mourning.

35For fire will come upon her from the Everlasting for many days,
and she will be inhabited by demons for a long time.

36Look toward the east, Jerusalem,
and see the joy that is coming to you from God.

37Here come your sons, whom you sent away;
they are coming, gathered from east to west
at the word of the Holy One,
rejoicing in the glory of God.

Notes

  • v1 "She is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endures forever" — wisdom is the law, as Sirach says at the end of Wisdom's own song, All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law that Moses commanded (Sirach 24:23). Will live… will die is the choice of Deuteronomy 30:15.

  • v4 "Happy are we, Israel" — Moses' last blessing, Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD (Deuteronomy 33:29), now said in the first person.

  • vv7–8 "by sacrificing to demons and not to God… You forgot the everlasting God, who brought you up" — the Song of Moses: They sacrificed to demons, not God, and you forgot the God who brought you forth in labor (Deuteronomy 32:17–18).

  • vv9–29 "Listen, you neighbors of Zion… a widow, forsaken by many" — Jerusalem speaks as a mother, the city of Lamentations who has become like a widow (Lamentations 1:1), now sending her children off and promising their return.

  • v15 "a nation from far away, a shameless nation of a strange language, who had no respect for the old and no pity for the child" — the curse of the law, a nation from far away… whose language you will not understand, a nation hard of face, who will not lift the face of the old or show favor to the young (Deuteronomy 28:49–50).

  • vv10, 14, 20, 22, 24, 35 "the Everlasting" — ho aiōnios, used here as a name for God, six times in the chapter, beside the Holy One (vv22, 37) and your everlasting Savior (v22).

  • vv20, 5:1 "I have taken off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth… Take off the garment of your mourning" — Jerusalem puts on mourning here, and in the next chapter is told to take it off.

  • vv30–35 "He who named you will comfort you… wretched is she who received your sons… inhabited by demons" — the comfort of Isaiah, Comfort, comfort My people (Isaiah 40:1), and the fate of the unnamed city that took the exiles, as in Isaiah's oracle on Babylon, where the Greek has demons for the goat-spirits of the Hebrew (Isaiah 13:21).

  • vv36–37 "Look toward the east, Jerusalem… Here come your sons" — Lift up your eyes all around and see: they all gather together, they come to you; your sons will come from afar (Isaiah 60:4).

chapters.title: Arise, Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Baruch 5

1Take off the garment of your mourning and affliction, Jerusalem,
and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God.

2Wrap yourself in the robe of the righteousness from God;
put on your head the turban of the glory of the Everlasting.

3For God will show your splendor to everything under heaven.

4For your name will be called by God forever:
"Peace of Righteousness" and "Glory of Godliness."

5Arise, Jerusalem, and stand on the height;
look toward the east,
and see your children gathered from west and east
at the word of the Holy One,
rejoicing that God has remembered them.

6For they went out from you on foot,
led away by their enemies;
but God brings them back to you,
carried in glory, as on a royal throne.

7For God has commanded that every high mountain
and the everlasting hills be made low,
and the valleys filled up to make the ground level,
so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God.

8The woods and every fragrant tree
have shaded Israel at God's command.

9For God will lead Israel with joy
in the light of His glory,
with the mercy and righteousness that come from Him.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Take off the garment of your mourning… put on the beauty of the glory from God… the robe of the righteousness from God" — Isaiah's call, put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city (Isaiah 52:1), and his song, He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness (Isaiah 61:10). The turban is the word of the high priest's headdress.

  • v4 "your name will be called by God forever: 'Peace of Righteousness' and 'Glory of Godliness'" — the new name Isaiah promised, you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give (Isaiah 62:2), and Jeremiah's name for the city, The LORD Is Our Righteousness (Jeremiah 33:16).

  • vv5–6 "see your children gathered… carried in glory, as on a royal throne" — 4:36–37 again. They left on foot, driven; they come back carried.

  • v7 "every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low, and the valleys filled up to make the ground level" — Isaiah's highway, Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill made low; the uneven ground shall become level (Isaiah 40:4).
